markdown: ## TL;DR The stale-evidence notice and its Refresh evidence button now disappear while a task's close-out is queued or running, and return if that close-out fails. The notice text is shortened to "Stale evidence", and the `repoos verify ` command text is gone from the card. Scoped `repoos check --changed main` passes. ## Work and rationale The card and drawer had two different gates. The card's stale block was gated only on `status === "review"` and a `STALE-EVIDENCE-ONLY` verdict (`staleEvidenceOnly` in `TaskCard.vue`). The drawer's Refresh evidence button was gated only on `status === "review"`. Neither looked at the integration pipeline, so a queued or running close-out still offered a button that starts a new review. I added one shared rule in `src/ui-app/src/lib/integration-pipeline-ui.ts`: `integrationEvidencePromptHidden(snap, taskId)`. It returns true when `integrationPipelineRole` reports the task as `queued`, or as `active` with a non-failed job. The job phases that count as non-terminal are exactly `queued`, `syncing`, `validating`, `publishing`, and `cleanup` (the `JobPhase` union in `src/server/integration-job.ts`, minus `done` and `failed`). Since the role already drops failed jobs, the rule covers the acceptance criteria without listing phases by hand. The card uses the helper inside `staleEvidenceOnly`, so the wrapper's `v-if` also goes false and the whole block disappears. The drawer gets a new `evidencePromptHidden` computed and adds `!evidencePromptHidden` to the Refresh evidence button's `v-if`. I did not reuse the drawer's existing `inPipeline` for this. It checks only `active.taskId` and `queue`, with no `failed` check, so a failed job would keep the button hidden. Changing it would also change the "Integrating…" UI that depends on it. The new computed leaves that path alone. The notice copy is now "Stale evidence". The `repoos verify` span is removed. The Refresh evidence button is unchanged. I left the CLI alone. `POST /api/tasks/:id/verify` already returns 409 "A close-out is active; wait for it to finish" when `closeOutLock.closingOut()` is true. That check fires only during an active close-out, not while a job sits in the queue. Closing that gap would be a separate server change. ## Approaches tried I considered gating on the phase names directly (`phase in {queued, syncing, …}`). That needs a second list that can drift from `JobPhase`. Because the only non-terminal phases are those five, testing for "in the pipeline and not failed" gives the same answer with less to maintain. I also considered hiding the card's notice in `TaskCard.vue` only and leaving the drawer alone. The task asked for both surfaces, so the drawer got the same rule. ## Challenges and blockers The first scoped check failed on a TypeScript error in my own new test. `wrapper.get(...)` throws when nothing matches, so `.exists()` on its result does not type-check. I switched that one assertion to `find(...)`. The re-run passed. The scoped check made WIP checkpoint commits on the branch (`WIP: engineer self-check checkpoint (#1277)`). AGENTS.md says these are expected. The branch diff against the task base holds only the six intended files. The first handoff failed UI verification. The automatic capture for `src/ui-app/**` targeted route `/`, which the router redirects to `/work` (`src/ui-app/src/router.ts`). That redirect predates this change. I fixed it by declaring a shot on `/work` with a new `card:staleEvidenceQueued` fixture (`src/core/shot-fixtures.ts` and `src/ui-app/src/lib/shot-preview-fixtures.ts`). The fixture seeds a stale-only review whose close-out is `validating`, and the shot highlights card 9999. The scoped `repoos check` then passed. ## Key learnings - A "hide while in pipeline" check needs to know whether a failed job still counts. The existing drawer `inPipeline` treats a failed active job as in pipeline. The card's `inPipeline` does not. Both are used elsewhere, so I did not change either. I wrote a separate rule instead. - `repoos check` runs `tests` on the remote validation runner (`REPOOS_SKIP_TESTS=1` locally), so the locally reported "skipped" is not a missing test run. I ran the three affected test files directly as well: 61 passing. - `needs-input-ui.ts` still tells users to run `repoos verify ` in a needs-input message. That is a different surface from the card and drawer, so I left it. It can be shortened in a follow-up if Nick wants the same wording there. ## Generated change summary Base tree: `9092b04a910901a594362620d3c76be7e2ad77b3` Source tree: `f5e1eec4faa37ae03a5e950ee5b45f3bba79eddb` - M src/core/shot-fixtures.ts: +2 / −0 - M src/ui-app/src/components/TaskCard.vue: +4 / −1 - M src/ui-app/src/components/TaskDrawer.vue: +7 / −1 - M src/ui-app/src/lib/integration-pipeline-ui.ts: +14 / −0 - M src/ui-app/src/lib/shot-preview-fixtures.ts: +30 / −0 - M src/ui-app/tests/integration-pipeline-ui.test.ts: +19 / −0 - M src/ui-app/tests/shot-preview-fixtures.test.ts: +12 / −0 - M src/ui-app/tests/task-card-review-verdict.test.ts: +82 / −2 - M src/ui-app/tests/task-drawer-ui-changes-rows.test.ts: +33 / −1
